description: Flat 8 m square of compacted red laterite earth with loose gravel and dried tyre ruts -- the unpaved Thai ground surface, as one quad and one seamless PBR texture set.

image.prompt:
A SEAMLESSLY TILING TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE. This is a flat material swatch, not a photograph of a scene or of an object. The camera looks straight down at the ground from directly overhead, perfectly orthographic, with no perspective, no horizon, no vanishing point and no tilt.

The surface: Flat square of compacted reddish brown laterite earth seen as a single unbroken surface, hard packed and rolled flat with loose gravel and small stones scattered over it, shallow dried tyre ruts and a few dried puddle hollows pressed into it, edge to edge bare earth only, no kerb, no border and no plants Materials: Seamlessly tiling rust-red and ochre laterite dirt, hard packed and dusty on the high ground with darker damp compacted earth in the hollows, loose tan and grey gravel and small broken stones scattered unevenly, shallow tyre ruts with a fine dust bloom along their edges, dried mud crack networks in the old puddle hollows, scattered dry leaf litter and a few motorcycle tread impressions; the surface must wrap on all four edges with no distinctive stone or rut repeating across a seam.

Scale: the square shown covers exactly 8 by 8 metres of real ground, so every stone, block, slab, joint, marking, rut and tuft in it is drawn at its true size relative to that. Do not zoom in on a detail and do not pull back to show a wider scene.

Tiling: the texture must repeat seamlessly on all four edges. What runs off the left edge continues onto the right edge, and what runs off the top continues onto the bottom, exactly. No feature may be cut in half at an edge without its other half appearing at the opposite edge. Laid out four by four this must read as one continuous surface with no visible grid, no repeated landmark feature and no seam.

Framing: the surface fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner. There is no border, no frame, no margin, no backdrop, no background, no matte and no empty space of any kind. The ground continues past every edge of the image.

Nothing stands on it and nothing bounds it: no kerb, no wall, no step, no gutter, no drain, no manhole cover, no grass verge, no plants, no people, no vehicles, no furniture, no objects, no litter, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows.

Lighting: flat, even, shadowless overhead illumination, like a lightbox. The image is the surface's true albedo. No sun, no cast shadows, no directional highlights, no specular blowout, no vignette, no gradient across the frame, no baked ambient occlusion in the corners and crevices, no light falloff towards the edges -- an uneven frame cannot tile, because its bright side would meet its dark side at every seam.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, realistic material, real surface wear and staining. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render preview, not a tiled collage of separate photographs, not a pattern illustration.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Compacted Laterite Dirt Tile
nameTh: พื้นดินลูกรัง
notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire surface reads out of the texture; the ruts, gravel and mud cracks are normal and AO relief, not geometry, and the tile is genuinely dead flat underfoot however deep the ruts look. This is a member of the kit's ground-surface tile set: every tile in that set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so it butts flush against any other ground tile and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside as a separate object. Laterite is the red earth of unsurfaced Thailand and it is what most of the country's ground actually is once the paving stops: rural and outer-suburban sois, construction sites and yards, temple and school grounds, market overflow parking, the verge beside any road that was surfaced without being widened. It is the tile that makes a scene read as somewhere rather than as a finished plaza, and it is the natural neighbour to the kit's construction and site props. Because the surface is irregular with no course or joint direction, it is fully FOUR-way rotationally symmetric -- it drops in at any of four orientations, which matters more here than on a patterned tile because a large unpaved area is exactly where a visible repeat is most obvious. The first thing to check on the generated texture is that no distinctive stone, rut or crack network appears twice across a seam. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. Quality refinement: reference-derived albedo retains fine grit; local rectangular source steps and low-frequency border colour are corrected. Independent Patina normals and packed AO/roughness fields now provide restrained dry-soil response. Eight img2threejs scopes accepted at visual estimate 96 after two corrections; installed 12-view parity and editor GLB pixel audits pass. PBR inference confidence .842, not calibrated physical depth. Exact single quad and one collision slab at y=0 retained. Evidence: scratch/compacted-laterite-dirt-tile/quality-above95/round02.
